role_and_message.evidence: The motivation remains noise-driven diversity before and after preference learning, with LR/HR and two reference methods for context.

panel_and_object_coverage.evidence: All ten original photograph tiles remain: LR, HR, SeeSR, OSEDiff, three NAOSD noises and three matching GDPO-SR noises.

labels_math_and_numbers.evidence: Noise1/2/3 labels retain their exact column pairings and method names; the original OSEDiff text is restored from source pixels to correct a generated spelling error.

connections_and_direction.evidence: NAOSD and GDPO-SR rows retain corresponding noise columns; the new downward after-preference-learning arrow expresses the source caption relation, not a per-image editing operation.

visual_encodings.evidence: Green/cyan/magenta noise encodings match both rows. All brick/roof texture differences are original evidence pixels rather than generated visual-quality changes.

examples_and_data.evidence: Independent checks confirm all ten tiles and original OSEDiff label are exact native1x RGB source copies with matching hashes.

unsupported_additions.evidence: Input/reference grouping and after-preference-learning annotation restate caption and first-two-page explanation. Same-noise heading refers to the source noise1/2/3 column correspondence, without new seed values.

complete_visible_content.evidence: All ten complete tiles and method/noise labels are visible and no output is covered by the restored OSEDiff label.

remaining_limitations: Original evidence pixels retain their source resolution; integer enlargement adds no information. Audit verifies fidelity to original caption/body, not reported scientific validity.
caption:
Figure 1. Noise regulates the diversity of generated samples. Different noise inputs yield both high-quality samples (e.g., noise1) and
low-quality ones (e.g., noise2 and noise3). After preference learning, the model produces more visually pleasing results.
